site_down.title: Your website did not load
site_down.why: Visitors and customers can't reach you right now.
how: Open your site on your phone using mobile data, not Wi-Fi, to confirm it is down for everyone.
Log in to your hosting or website builder account and look for a status or outage notice.
Check that your domain and hosting plans haven't expired; renewal emails often go to an old inbox.
If it is still down after an hour, contact your host's support and give them the error shown in this report.

domain_not_found.title: Your domain name is not pointing anywhere
domain_not_found.why: The web address doesn't lead to a server, which usually means an expired domain or a DNS change.
how: Log in where you bought your domain and check that it is active and set to renew.
Check its DNS settings still point to your website host. Your host's help pages list the right values.
DNS changes can take a few hours to spread, so check again later the same day.

domain_expiring_30.title: Your domain name expires within a month
domain_expiring_30.why: If it lapses, your website and any email on that domain stop working, and someone else could register it.
how: Log in where you bought your domain and check that auto-renew is on and the card on file is current.
If auto-renew is off, renew it now, ideally for more than one year.

domain_expiring_60.title: Your domain name expires within two months
domain_expiring_60.why: A quick check now avoids a scramble later.
how: Log in where you bought your domain and confirm auto-renew is on and the payment card hasn't expired.

cert_invalid.title: Your security certificate has a problem
cert_invalid.why: Browsers show visitors a full-page warning, and most people leave.
how: Open your site in a browser and read the exact warning.
In your hosting or website builder dashboard, find the SSL or HTTPS setting and renew or reissue the certificate.
Most hosts include free certificates that renew automatically; make sure auto-renew is switched on.
If you recently changed your domain, ask your host to issue a certificate that covers the new name and the www version.

cert_expiring_14.title: Your security certificate expires within 2 weeks
cert_expiring_14.why: Once it expires, browsers show a warning page instead of your site.
how: Log in to your host and check that the certificate is set to renew automatically.
If renewal is manual, renew it today.
Next week's check will confirm the new expiry date.

cert_expiring_30.title: Your security certificate expires within a month
cert_expiring_30.why: Most certificates renew on their own, but it is worth confirming before it becomes urgent.
how: Check your hosting dashboard for the certificate's renewal setting.
If it renews automatically, there's nothing to do. Next week's check will show the new date.

no_https_redirect.title: The http:// version of your site doesn't switch to https://
no_https_redirect.why: Visitors who type your address without https see a "Not secure" label.
how: In your hosting or website builder settings, find "Force HTTPS", "Always use HTTPS" or a similar switch and turn it on.
Then open http://yourdomain in a private browser window and check that it lands on https://.

alt_host_broken.title: The www (or non-www) version of your address doesn't work
alt_host_broken.why: Some people type www and some don't. Both should reach your site.
how: In your domain's DNS settings, make sure both the bare domain and www point to your host.
In your host's domain settings, set one as the main address and redirect the other to it.

noindex_home.title: Your homepage tells search engines not to list it
noindex_home.why: A "noindex" tag hides your homepage from search results. This is often left on by mistake after a site launch.
how: In your website builder, look for a setting like "Hide from search engines", "Discourage search engines" or "Search engine visibility" and switch it off.
If a developer built the site, ask them to remove the noindex robots tag from the homepage.

noindex_page.title: Some pages tell search engines not to list them
noindex_page.why: That is fine for private pages, but not for pages you want customers to find.
how: Look at the pages listed. For each one you want found, turn off the page's "hide from search" option.

robots_blocks_all.title: Your robots.txt file blocks all search engines
robots_blocks_all.why: A rule of "Disallow: /" for every crawler keeps your whole site out of search.
how: Turn off any "Discourage search engines" setting in your website builder.
If you edit robots.txt yourself, remove the "Disallow: /" line under "User-agent: *".

broken_internal.title: Broken links inside your site
broken_internal.why: Visitors who click these hit an error page, and search engines notice too.
how: Open each page listed under "found on" and find the link.
Point it to the right page, or remove it if the page is gone.
If you moved or renamed a page, add a redirect from the old address to the new one in your site settings.

broken_external.title: Links to other websites that no longer work
broken_external.why: They make your site look out of date.
how: Open the page listed under "found on", then update or remove the link.

missing_title.title: A page has no title
missing_title.why: The title is the headline search engines show for your page.
how: In your website builder, open the page's SEO or page settings.
Add a title of about 50 to 60 characters: what the page offers plus your business name and town.

title_length.title: A page title is very short or very long
title_length.why: Long titles get cut off in search results; very short ones say too little.
how: Aim for about 50 to 60 characters: what the page offers, plus your business name.

missing_description.title: A page has no meta description
missing_description.why: The description is often the snippet people read under your link in search results.
how: In the page's SEO settings, write one or two sentences (about 120 to 160 characters) on what visitors will find and why it is worth a click.

description_length.title: A meta description is very short or very long
description_length.why: Very short descriptions say little; long ones get cut off.
how: Aim for about 120 to 160 characters.

missing_h1.title: A page has no main heading
missing_h1.why: A clear main heading (H1) helps visitors and search engines understand the page.
how: Give each page one main heading at the top, using the "Heading 1" style in your editor.

multiple_h1.title: A page has more than one main heading
multiple_h1.why: One main heading per page keeps the outline clear.
how: Keep one "Heading 1" and change the others to "Heading 2".

missing_viewport.title: A page isn't set up for phones
missing_viewport.why: Without a viewport tag, phones show a tiny zoomed-out page.
how: Most modern themes include this. If yours doesn't, ask your developer to add the standard viewport meta tag, or switch to a mobile-friendly theme.

missing_lang.title: A page doesn't declare its language
missing_lang.why: Screen readers and translation tools use it.
how: Set your site language in your website builder's general settings.

images_missing_alt.title: Images without alt text
images_missing_alt.why: Alt text describes an image for people using screen readers, and helps search engines.
how: In your editor, click each image listed and fill in its alt text or image description: a short, plain description of what it shows.
Purely decorative images can have empty alt text.

mixed_content.title: Some files load over insecure http://
mixed_content.why: Browsers may block them or show a "Not secure" warning.
how: Change the listed image, script or style addresses from http:// to https://.
If the file isn't available over https, upload it to your own site instead.

duplicate_titles.title: Several pages share the same title
duplicate_titles.why: Search engines can't tell them apart.
how: Give each page its own title that says what is on that page.

no_sitemap.title: No sitemap found
no_sitemap.why: A sitemap lists your pages so search engines can find them all.
how: Most website builders make one automatically at /sitemap.xml; check it is switched on.
Then add it to your robots.txt file with a line like "Sitemap: https://yourdomain/sitemap.xml".

no_robots.title: No robots.txt file
no_robots.why: It isn't required, but it is the usual place to point search engines to your sitemap.
how: Many builders create one for you; look for a robots.txt setting.

no_favicon.title: No site icon (favicon)
no_favicon.why: The small icon in browser tabs and bookmarks makes your site easy to spot.
how: Upload a square version of your logo as the site icon or favicon in your website builder's settings.

no_og_image.title: No social sharing image
no_og_image.why: When someone shares your link, there is no picture in the preview.
how: In your site's SEO or social settings, set a default sharing image, ideally 1200 by 630 pixels.

no_local_schema.title: No local business details for search engines
no_local_schema.why: Structured data can help search engines show your hours, address and phone.
how: Many builders and SEO add-ons have a "Local business" or "Business details" section; fill it in.
Keep the details exactly the same as on your Google Business Profile.

slow_load.title: Your homepage is slow to load
slow_load.why: Slow pages lose visitors, especially on phones and mobile data.
how: Shrink large images before uploading (most photos only need to be about 1600 pixels wide).
Remove add-ons, sliders, chat widgets or embeds you don't really need.
Ask your host whether caching and compression are switched on.

heavy_page.title: Your homepage is heavy
heavy_page.why: A heavy page takes longer to load and uses up visitors' mobile data.
how: Start with the largest files listed in this report and resize or compress them.
Use one or two photos at the top of the page rather than a large gallery or video that plays on load.

slow_ttfb.title: Your server is slow to respond
slow_ttfb.why: The first byte of your homepage took a long time to arrive.
how: Turn on your host's caching option if it has one.
If it stays slow week after week, ask your host about a faster plan or server.

not_compressed.title: Your pages aren't compressed
not_compressed.why: Compression makes pages download faster for free.
how: Ask your host to turn on gzip or Brotli compression; many hosts have a switch for it.

large_files.title: Very large files on your homepage
large_files.why: Big images or scripts slow down the first visit.
how: Resize or compress the files listed. Image files under about 300 KB are a good target.

security_headers.title: Missing security settings
security_headers.why: A few standard settings help protect visitors. They are worth asking your host or developer about.
how: Share the list of missing settings in this report with your host or developer and ask them to add them.

stale_content.title: Your site hasn't had a visible update in a while
stale_content.why: Fresh news, photos or offers show customers you are open and active.
how: Add something new: a seasonal offer, a recent photo, an updated menu or an event.

copyright_old.title: The year in your footer is out of date
copyright_old.why: An old year can make visitors wonder if you are still open.
how: Update the copyright year in your footer, or ask your developer to make it update automatically.

phone_not_on_home.title: Your phone number isn't on your homepage
phone_not_on_home.why: Many customers visit just to call you.
how: Add your phone number to the header or footer so it appears on every page. Make it tappable on phones.

street_not_on_home.title: Your address isn't on your homepage
street_not_on_home.why: Customers looking for directions expect to find it quickly.
how: Add your address to the footer, matching your Google Business Profile exactly.

gbp_reminders.text: Check your Google Business Profile hours, and add special hours for any holiday or closure in the next month.
Add one or two fresh photos to your Google Business Profile: your storefront, your team or something new.
Reply to any new Google reviews, good or bad, briefly and politely.
Post a short update or offer on your Google Business Profile.
Check that your Google Business Profile phone, website address and categories still match your site.
Check the products or services listed on your Google Business Profile are current.
